items.title: Government considering military assistance request from Gulf States
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong says the government is considering requests for military assistance from Gulf countries targeted by Iranian attacks.

items.title: Live: Iran can fight 'intense war' for six months, Revolutionary Guard says
items.description: Donald Trump says the US and Israel will hit Iran "very hard" after Tehran rejected his demand for surrender.  Follow live.

items.title: Hemmed in by wars, here's how some airlines are still flying from Australia to Europe
items.description: Travel routes between Australia, Asia and Europe are narrowing. Here is how airlines are still flying the Kangaroo route despite wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.

items.title: Live: Oscar Piastri crashes and is out before the Aus GP
items.description: Oscar Piastri will not start the Australian Grand Prix after he crashed his car on the way to the grid. Follow live.

items.title: Will higher fuel prices drive EV uptake? We crunched the numbers
items.description: As deepening conflict in the Middle East causes fuel prices to rise, will EVs boom? We've compared operating costs to see how they compare to petrol cars.

items.title: A fall, a fracture and a death that didn’t add up
items.description: Attila's shaky phone video of his brother lying dead in aged care documented bruises and blood. It was the start of a long campaign to understand what happened.

items.title: Katherine suffers worst flooding in 28 years as NT residents await rescue
items.description: Katherine experienced its worst flooding in 28 years overnight, while several Territorians stranded in a nearby remote community are currently waiting on helicopter rescues.

items.title: Uncomfortable truths for Australia as a middle power
items.description: Middle powers may have a larger role to play in the emerging world order, but the same old dilemma persists: how far are they willing to defend the rules when the countries bending them are their closest allies?

items.title: A pristine tourist hotspot is being preserved by those who love it most
items.description: This tiny community is enduring the ultimate balancing act, keeping hordes of tourists happy, mitigating the impacts of climate change and protecting their World Heritage-listed home. Lisa Millar explores how Shark Bay not only survives, but thrives.

items.title: After 75 years of Coalition rule, Farrer's voters are ready to flip
items.description: The upcoming Farrer by-election is already being talked about as a litmus test for the new opposition leader and an ascendant One Nation. It'll also be a measure of major party politics.

items.title: Notorious UK child killer Ian Huntley dies after prison attack
items.description: Ian Huntley had been on life support after being hit over the head with a metal bar at Frankland prison in north-east England.

items.title: Three charged with murdering Good Samaritan at Melbourne railway station
items.description: Two teenagers and a man have been charged after 22-year-old Aidan Becker died from stab wounds in Mernda on Friday night. Police are waiting to interview a fourth person about the death.

items.title: Rock fishermen drown amid 'very choppy' conditions on NSW Central Coast
items.description: Emergency services find the bodies of two Sydney men after being called to Little Beach, at Bouddi National Park.

items.title: Bringing old Aussie homes into an energy efficient future
items.description: Owners of older homes are being urged to have their energy efficiency assessed, with experts saying improvements will not only make them more comfortable, but help them save money as well.

items.title: Are couples happier sleeping separately?
items.description: Despite many people like Hannah finding a "sleep divorce" improves their sleep — and their relationship — a "pervasive stigma" about not sharing a bed persists.

items.title: Insist you're the best at trivia all you want — I know the truth
items.description: I'm so glad you're back for another round! Just kidding, as if I'd ever say that. Let's play, HARD!

items.title: The K-pop concert that sparked an online war across Asia
items.description: Criticism of Korean fans bringing professional cameras into a Korean boy band concert in Malaysia, against local rules, spiralled into an online war from Vietnam to Indonesia.

items.title: Matildas hope other Asian nations don't have to keep fighting for the basics
items.description: There was a time when the Matildas had to fight and scrap for pay, recognition, and respect. They hope the Women's Asian Cup can change things for other nations.

items.title: 'You had to think on your feet': How Ranger Stacey became loved by Australian kids
items.description: Nineties kids didn't dawdle on the way home from school in the afternoon. This was the age of appointment television, and that appointment was with Ranger Stacey on Totally Wild.

items.title: SA government attributes email to wrong man after death, traumatising family
items.description: A grieving woman "feels sick" after the government releases an email it claims was written by her deceased partner praising his hospital care, after she said ambulance ramping had denied him dignity in his final hours.

items.title: After 4 years, regional gallery reopens with blockbuster exhibition
items.description: Newcastle Art Gallery celebrates its $48 million expansion with a landmark show drawn from its permanent collection, which features more than 7,000 works valued at $145 million.

items.title: Reclaiming humanity post Bondi attack
items.description: Michael Visontay explores the deep roots of Jewish life in Bondi, and the impact of loss on this close-knit community.

items.title: Promises ramped down in SA election as ambulance crisis proves hard to solve
items.description: With just two weeks to go until the state election, Labor has steered away from ambitious promises after difficulty meeting its pledge to fix the ambulance ramping crisis last election — one of the few points where the opposition's barbs are piercing.

items.title: Fire crews attend second RSL fire in Melbourne in three days
items.description: An RSL in Glen Waverley has been significantly damaged by fire in the second club blaze this week.

items.title: All-ages heavy metal gigs offering 'freedom' for youths after COVID lockdowns
items.description: In community halls across Western Sydney young people are headbanging, crowdsurfing and forming mosh pits.
